been there a few times now, and if it's not one thing, it's another.

The most recent issue was an appointment booked by the healthcare assistant who does the morning blood tests. She's amazing, but she scheduled me for a test I was pretty sure I didn’t need, as it's only done every few years. I mentioned it to her but figured she’s the professional, and if I truly didn’t need it, someone would probably catch it before the day.

So, I show up at 8am for the appointment. After waiting 10–15 minutes in an empty waiting room, I’m finally called in, only to be told I shouldn't be there. When I challenged the nurse (someone different to whom booked me in), she explained she only works Thursdays, so she wouldn’t have seen it, and apparently neither did reception because they have no access to those records.

I don’t know what system they’re using, but as a nurse, you should check in advance, specially when this already happened before (she told me), and maybe sit down and give some training to the assistant.
I work with calendars and always double-check things to avoid issues like this. Every time I go there, it feels like there's a lack of accountability, poor training, no desire to evolve, and plenty of finger-pointing.

My experience with the doctors has still been positive, though I’ve only spoken with them over the phone, and the healthcare assistant is extremely
